author: Forbes
description:
How do you build a multi-billion-dollar tech unicorn by completely rewriting a generational, 80-year-old industry?

In this interview, ForbesWomen Editor Maggie McGrath, sits with Ritu Narayan, the co-founder and CEO of Zum, shares the incredible story of how she set out to solve a deeply personal parenting challenge and ended up modernizing the largest mass transit system in America. From her early days of personally driving the school vehicles to navigating a high-stakes pivot from an "Uber for kids" model to the "AWS for student transportation," Narayan explains how she scaled Zoom to over $2.6 billion in total contract value. She also opens up about surviving a crucible moment just three weeks from running out of money, solving the national school bus driver shortage, and why she believes being an "underdog" over the age of 50 is her absolute greatest advantage.

author: Forbes
description:
Can Wall Street strategies actually rebuild the American dream? In this interview, ForbesWomen Editor Maggie McGrath speaks with Tracy Palandjian, co-founder and CEO of Social Finance, about how she is flipping traditional philanthropy on its head.

After starting her venture at age 39 as a working mother of three, Palandjian has spent the last 15 years mobilizing over $500 million to drive economic mobility across America. She shares how Social Finance acts as a bridge between markets and mission, leveraging innovative financial models like outcomes-based nursing student loans, home equity recovery strategies, and a historic $150 million AI fellowship with Anthropic. 

Palandjian also details her remarkable personal journey—from secretly applying to US boarding schools as a teenager in Hong Kong to receiving the Ellis Island Medal of Honor—and why she believes getting older is a major advantage in business and life.

0:00 Bringing Wall Street Rigor To Social Impact
3:05 Rewriting Deb
title: How This CEO Mobilized $500 Million For Social Good

author: Forbes
description:
From making her highly anticipated Broadway debut to building a global haircare empire, Tracee Ellis Ross is redefining what it means to step into your ultimate power after 50.

ForbesWomen Editor, Maggie McGrath, sits with Ellis Ross as she shares a wonderfully candid look at her summer Broadway debut in Every Brilliant Thing, revealing how she transforms terror into pure excitement and why she embraces the vulnerability of a completely illuminated, participating audience. She also opens up about the tenacious 10-year journey to launch Pattern Beauty, how she proved the industry wrong by serving an underserved global market, and why doing the right thing is actually "quite lucrative" in business. Above all, Ellis Ross delivers an inspiring, joyful masterclass on why she has always loved getting older, why she wouldn't return to her 20s if you paid her, and what it truly feels like to finally belong to yourself.

0:00 Transforming Fear And The Broadway Debut
4:06 Building Pattern Beau
title: How Tracee Ellis Ross Proved The Beauty Industry Wrong

From Hollywood superstar to co-founding a public company, Jennifer Garner is redefining what it means to build a mission-driven empire after 50. Editor of ForbesWomen, Maggie McGrath sits with Garner as she opens up about the historic IPO of her organic food brand, Once Upon a Farm, and explains why she completely ignores the daily stock price to keep her eyes on the true prize: driving systemic change in childhood nutrition. 

She candidly shares her experience of learning how to read spreadsheets from scratch, her 18 years of deeply personal advocacy work fighting rural childhood hunger with Save the Children, and why she believes being over 50 makes her more fully realized, empathetic, and hungrier than ever for the future.

How do you go from working grueling 100-hour weeks as a corporate M&A lawyer to building an audience of over 20 million followers and running a multi-faceted financial media business?

Welcome to the Forbes Top Creator Show! This week, host Steven Bertoni decodes the business of influence with attorney, financial creator, and entrepreneur Erika Kullberg.

In this episode, Erika opens up about the heartbreaking turning point that led her to quit her big-firm corporate law job after her boss refused her time off to see her dying grandfather. She details her transition from $200,000 in student debt to launching her startup, Plug and Law. Erika delivers a true masterclass on how she systematically studied YouTube and TikTok like an M&A deal, writing down over 100 viral hooks to decode the rhythm of the algorithm.
